scenarios.title: Orientation Email Link
scenarios.summary: A new-student orientation email asks you to confirm your school account through a shortened link.
scenarios.promptText: You receive an email saying your enrollment will be delayed unless you confirm your student credentials immediately.
scenarios.educationalObjective: Recognize urgency tactics and verify links before entering credentials.
scenarios.narrativeContext: The player is exploring campus and checks a mobile inbox.

choices.choiceText: Open the link and sign in immediately.
choices.feedbackText: The message used urgency to pressure you into acting before verifying it.
choices.outcomeText: Your credentials are harvested and your cyber status drops.

choices.choiceText: Check the sender address and open the school portal manually in a browser.
choices.feedbackText: Independent verification is the safest way to handle suspicious login requests.
choices.outcomeText: You avoid the phishing attempt and strengthen your trust score.

choices.choiceText: Forward the message to classmates and ask if they got it too.
choices.feedbackText: Sharing suspicious content can spread the threat and does not verify legitimacy.
choices.outcomeText: The threat remains unresolved and confidence in your response drops.

scenarios.title: Unlabeled USB Drive
scenarios.summary: You find an unlabeled USB drive beside a computer in the campus lab.
scenarios.promptText: The drive might belong to another student, but it could also contain malware or a trap.
scenarios.educationalObjective: Avoid unknown removable media and report it safely.
scenarios.narrativeContext: The player is in a classroom computer lab.

choices.choiceText: Plug it into the nearest workstation to identify the owner.
choices.feedbackText: Unknown removable devices are a common malware delivery vector.
choices.outcomeText: The workstation is compromised and your cyber status falls.

choices.choiceText: Turn it in to the lab supervisor without plugging it in.
choices.feedbackText: Escalating unknown devices is the correct control action.
choices.outcomeText: The device is handled safely and your trust score improves.

choices.choiceText: Take it home and check it on your personal laptop.
choices.feedbackText: Moving the device to another system still exposes you to risk.
choices.outcomeText: You extend the risk to another environment.
